stories.story: On Thursday, the music room filled with wandering piano scales and sleepy flute notes; Nia noticed the little drum on the shelf; its red ribbon rested against the handle. She wanted a duet for Saturday with a drumbeat and an answering part. Dalia lent Nia the drum for the week, its red ribbon bright against the wooden rim. Nia asked Mateo if he might play the answering part with her at the picnic. Mateo said that he enjoyed music, though he was not ready for a public performance. Then Nia practiced the drum pattern on the rug, making room for an answer, the red ribbon quivering against the rim. Dalia set the signup sheet beside the piano, announcing that the program had room for one more act. Then Nia wrote only her own name on the signup sheet, choosing a drum solo and leaving the public choice with Mateo. On Saturday, folding chairs crowded the room as Dalia introduced the solo; she played two quick beats and a wide pause, then filled the pause with quieter beats. She asked Mateo whether he wanted to try the answering part privately on the rug after the crowd thinned. Then Mateo said he would rather listen than play; she left the choice with him without asking again. Nia returned the borrowed drum to the shelf, the red ribbon settling against the wooden rim. The borrowed drum rested beside the untouched second drum on the shelf; the program still named Nia alone, and Mateo choice stayed his.

Amid the piano scales and long flute notes in the music room; Nia spotted the little drum beside the shelf; its red ribbon rested against the handle. She hoped a duet for Saturday where one beat could invite another. Dalia lent Nia the drum for the week, its red ribbon bright against the wooden rim. Nia asked Mateo if he might play the answering part with her at the picnic. Mateo said that he enjoyed music, though he was not ready for a public performance. Nia practiced the drum pattern on the rug, making room for an answer, the red ribbon bobbing with each stroke. Dalia set the signup sheet beside the piano, announcing that the program had room for one more act. Nia wrote only her own name on the signup sheet, choosing a drum solo and leaving the public choice with Mateo. Before the waiting rows of chairs, Dalia introduced Nia drum solo; Nia played two quick beats and a wide pause, then filled the pause with quieter beats. She asked Mateo whether he wanted to try the answering part privately on the rug after the crowd thinned. Mateo agreed to try a private duet on the rug, choosing the answering part for himself. Then he crossed to the shelf and picked up the second drum to carry it to the rug. He joined Nia on the rug with one testing answer beat; Nia left room for two more. Nia returned the borrowed drum to the shelf, the red ribbon quivering as the last sound faded. Mateo returned the second drum to the shelf, both instruments back where they belonged. The two drums rested side by side on the shelf, their unlisted duet fading beneath the room quiet sounds.
